items.q: Who is A Better Tomorrow Social for?
items.a: ABT is for women in Houston who want to meet people and give back locally. You might find us at a cocktail soirée, packing meals or heading to Pilates.

items.q: How do I get tickets to a social?
items.a: Check the link in our Instagram bio for the next event and its booking details. Our ticketed socials use Eventbrite; availability depends on the event.
Past gatherings have supported Daya Houston, Houston Food Bank and The Avondale House through fundraising, donated items and volunteering. Check the event post for the cause and donation details.

items.q: How do I become a member?
items.a: Send us a membership inquiry using the form below, or DM us on Instagram. The form gives us a little background about you; it doesn’t book a ticket or confirm membership.

items.q: Can my business sponsor or partner with ABT?
items.a: We’d love to hear from local businesses, venues and nonprofit organizations. Choose the business or partner option in the form and leave your contact details.

items.q: Do I need to bring anything?
items.a: Check the event post before you come. Some socials include a donation drive, like the hygiene items collected at Galentine’s. You’ll find the dress code there too.

socials.title: Galentine’s Soirée
socials.blurb: Pink and red cocktail attire, a bouquet bar and an evening at Sophie’s Living Room. Our Galentine’s Soirée raised funds and collected hygiene items for Daya Houston.

socials.title: Day of Service & Sisterhood
socials.blurb: We spent the morning at Houston Food Bank, packing nearly 16,000 meals for families in need. Then we sat down for lunch, mimosas and a chance to catch up.

slides.alt: Members at the Houston Food Bank sign

socials.title: Pilates Charity Social
socials.blurb: A Pilates class at Jetset River Oaks supporting The Avondale House, which serves people with autism and other disabilities. Movement, mindfulness and time together.

story.lead: A Better Tomorrow Social brings women together in Houston to make friends and support local causes.
body: We meet over cocktails, on the volunteer line and in the Pilates studio. There’s time to get to know each other, and a reason for getting together beyond the social itself.
Our gatherings have supported Daya Houston, Houston Food Bank and The Avondale House. That has meant fundraising, donated hygiene items and a morning spent packing nearly 16,000 meals.
